title: The magi and the flight (Matthew 2:1–23)
hook: strangers from the east follow a star, then the family runs to Egypt as refugees
tomorrow: how do you lose a twelve-year-old for three whole days?

segments.voice: That was the week of the child: a doorway, a song, a silent man, no room, the night shift, and two who waited. Yesterday's line: waiting is not wasted.
screen: `WAITING IS NOT WASTED.` → `THE WEEK OF THE CHILD.`

segments.voice: Your maps app says nine hours. Would you drive that to see a baby you'd never met, in a country that isn't yours? Matthew says strangers did more: magi from the east, following a star into Jerusalem and asking, in the Douay-Rheims Bible, "Where is he that is born king of the Jews? For we have seen his star in the east, and are come to adore him." King Herod hears it, and Matthew says he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
screen: `NINE HOURS FOR A STRANGER'S BABY?` → `WHERE IS HE THAT IS BORN KING?` → `HEROD IS LISTENING.`

segments.voice: The star brings them to the house in Bethlehem. They kneel and open their treasures: gold, frankincense and myrrh. Now what Matthew doesn't say. He never says three; tradition counted three, likely from the gifts. He never calls them kings, and Caspar, Melchior and Balthasar are names from later tradition. They're foreigners, the first in Matthew's Gospel to worship Jesus. So the feast is the Epiphany, from the Greek for a showing: Christ shown to the whole world. One to tell a friend: an old Epiphany custom chalks the new year over the front door around the letters C, M and B, the magi's traditional initials and a Latin blessing, may Christ bless this house. Then the story turns. Joseph, the man who never speaks, dreams again: "Arise, and take the child and his mother, and fly into Egypt." They leave by night, across a border. Herod orders the killing of Bethlehem's baby boys, whom the Church remembers as the Holy Innocents. Pope Pius the Twelfth called the exiled Holy Family the model of every family forced to flee.
screen: `NOT THREE, NOT KINGS: MAGI.` · `EPIPHANY — SHOWN TO THE WORLD.` · `C + M + B OVER THE DOOR.` · `ARISE, AND FLY INTO EGYPT.` · then, large: `THE HOLY FAMILY WERE REFUGEES.`

segments.voice: Stand up and hold out your hands as if each could carry one thing on a night you had to leave home: which two things would you take? Keep that posture while you think of one family somewhere who left like that, as Mary and Joseph did. If you pray, you can pray for them in the name of the Holy Family; if not, just hold them in mind and hope for them.
Epiphany. A showing: Christ revealed to strangers from the east, before his own family runs for their lives.
Pocket this one: the holy family were refugees, strangers in Egypt until Herod was gone. Four weeks, done.

screen: `DAY 28 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: HOW DO YOU LOSE A TWELVE-YEAR-OLD FOR THREE DAYS?`

howItsDone: Catholics celebrate the Epiphany on January 6 or the nearest Sunday; in many places the door is blessed with chalk, and the Church remembers the Holy Innocents on December 28.

Epiphany.meaning: from the Greek for a showing: Christ revealed to the world

magi.meaning: Matthew's word for the strangers from the east

Herod.meaning: the king in Jerusalem when Jesus was born

frankincense.meaning: a sweet-smelling resin burned as incense

myrrh.meaning: a fragrant resin, one of the magi's gifts

Holy Innocents.meaning: the baby boys of Bethlehem killed on Herod's order

sources.ref: Rituale Romanum: blessing of chalk on the Epiphany; the C+M+B door inscription (Christus mansionem benedicat)

notes: Matthew 2:2 and 2:13 quoted from Douay-Rheims; confirm exact wording.
Magi as star-watchers from Persia or Babylon: common scholarly view; confirm.
Herod killing members of his own family (a wife and sons, per Josephus): stated simply; confirm.
The massacre of the innocents is recorded only in Matthew; mentioned briefly and without dramatization. Confirm.
Pius XII's Exsul Familia opens by calling the Holy Family in exile the archetype of every refugee family; paraphrased. Confirm.
The outline practice 'pray for one refugee family' is offered as an invitation with a non-praying alternative.
